summary: Stream-transform package: defines the StreamTransform protocol (wrap encodes, unwrap decodes, both lazily over binary streams) and two implementations, Gzip (stdlib, reproducible mtime=0, decompression bounded to 1 GiB by default) and GPG (python-gnupg via the [encryption] extra, fully buffered). It also hosts materialize(), an opt-in helper that drains a stream into a seekable memory or spooled-tempfile buffer and returns its length. Pipeline is re-exported here but profiled as its own module.
key_classes: StreamTransform — runtime-checkable protocol with wrap(stream)->BinaryIO (encode) and unwrap(stream)->BinaryIO (decode)
Gzip — gzip transform; wrap streams compression via GzipCompressingReader, unwrap returns a bounded GzipFile (forward-only reader over non-seekable input)
_BoundedGzipFile — GzipFile subclass capping every read/readline/seek at max_decompressed_bytes and raising TransformError past it
GPG — encrypts on wrap (requires recipients) and decrypts on unwrap via python-gnupg; result buffered in BytesIO
key_functions: Gzip(level=6, mtime=0, max_decompressed_bytes=1024**3) — construct; None disables the decode bound
GPG(recipients=None, gnupghome=None, key_file=None, passphrase=None, armor=False, always_trust=False) — construct; client and key import are lazy on first use
materialize(stream, *, to='memory'|'tempfile', memory_cutoff=64 MiB) -> tuple[BinaryIO, int] — drain a stream into a seekable buffer and return (buffer, length)
extension_points: Implement the StreamTransform protocol (wrap/unwrap returning readable BinaryIO, lazy, leaving borrowed inputs open on read) to add a new codec; Pipeline accepts any conforming object
Register new suffixes for read-side inference in storage/path_helpers/suffixes.py (outside this module) when adding a codec
lifecycle_notes: Gzip is stdlib-only and imports on a base install; GPG imports gnupg lazily in _get_client() and raises ImportError naming [encryption] when missing (not MissingExtraError).
GPG caches its gnupg client and imports key_file once per instance.
Gzip.unwrap over a non-seekable source returns a forward-only BufferedReader; over a seekable source it returns the seekable (bounded) GzipFile.
The write-side GzipCompressingReader closes its source on close(), unlike the read-side contract where transforms leave borrowed inputs open.
materialize() exhausts the input stream and returns a buffer positioned at 0; the caller owns both.
documentation_hooks: Stream transforms guide: Gzip and GPG options, reproducible output, decompression-bomb bound
Writing a custom StreamTransform (protocol contract, laziness, ownership)

risks: GPG buffers the full payload in memory on both wrap and unwrap (encryption.py docstring) and has no decrypted-size bound analogous to Gzip's max_decompressed_bytes.
GPG stores passphrase as a plain instance attribute; encryption.py carries a '#TERCHDEBT: Need to use GPGHelper here!' marker and has had no commits since the June 2026 reorganisation.
GPG missing-extra path raises plain ImportError, inconsistent with the package-wide MissingExtraError convention (AGENTS.md Dependencies).
materialize() is documented in AGENTS.md and docs/read-access-modes.md but lives at the private path _core.transforms.util and is not exported from the package root or transforms __all__.
Gzip default 1 GiB bound can surprise users reading large trusted archives; they must pass max_decompressed_bytes=None or a larger value.
open_questions: Should materialize() be promoted to a public export (root or transforms __all__), given it is referenced in user docs?
Should GPG raise MissingExtraError and gain a decode size bound to match Gzip?
Should GzipCompressingReader.close() leave its source open to match the read-side borrowed-input contract?
